claims.assertion: This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (total $25.40 in F9), so any route-deviation refund is limited to metered distance units at the trip's per-km rate, and waiting time is chargeable per the meter.
The 14:10–14:13 off-route segment (F4, +1.63 km) is exempt because the driver proposed the Cavenagh reroute at 14:01 and the rider agreed at 14:02, both before the segment began at 14:10.

The reroute was justified: an accident was reported at 13:52 only 30 m from the optimal route (two lanes closed, Orchard Road towards Bras Basah after Cavenagh), reported before the trip window and still listed during it.

Traffic conditions corroborate the driver's decision: Orchard Road was at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h, severe congestion) for 14:00–14:10, exactly the pickup window when the driver was leaving Orchard Road.

The rider asked for a 7-Eleven stop and the driver accepted (F11, F12), so the stop itself was a passenger-requested detour; the 4 min 10 s stationary period at 14:20–14:24 (F2) corresponds to that stop.
The waiting time of 4.2 minutes billed as $1.08 (F7) is meter waiting time on a RydeTAXI trip and is chargeable to the rider, not refundable.

The refund the rider can properly claim is confined to the unexempted portion of the 14:17–14:29 segment: 2.83 km of extra distance at $1.41/km = $3.99, since the 1.63 km segment at F4 is covered by the rider's agreement (F11).

Even under the rider's best case, the total excess distance billed of $7.58 (F6) overstates the refundable amount: the metered fare is lawfully chargeable for all distance actually driven after a passenger-requested stop, and the driver had reasonable cause for the Orchard Road avoidance.

The driver's profile shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 days and it was a no-show, not a route dispute (route: 0), so RD-6's repeated-route-violation condition is not met and no account flag should attach on that basis.

weaknesses: The 14:17–14:29 segment (F5) added 2.83 km with the vehicle up to 1553 m from the optimal route, and the chat only shows agreement to go 'by Cavenagh' (F10, F11) — the rider will argue Beach Road was outside the scope of that consent, which RD-5 addresses against the driver.

The rider's chat (F11) asked for 'a 7-Eleven on the way', not Beach Road, so under RD-3(b) the driver's self-chosen Beach Road stop may not exempt the extra kilometres on that segment; the driver's statement (F13) that he chose the 7-Eleven he knew on Beach Road is a statement only, and the GPS (F2) places the stop 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off.

The trip took 26.5 min against an 8 min estimate (F3) with actual distance 9.3 km vs 3.9 km optimal (F1), a +136% deviation — the rider will use F1 and F3 to argue the overall routing was not 'shortest and most direct' regardless of the accident.

The traffic band evidence for the specific alternative taken is thin: Orchard Road band 1 (F14) and the accident (F17) support avoiding Orchard Road, but Bayfront Avenue band 3 and Bras Basah band 4 (F15, F16) do not show severe congestion on the replaced optimal-route portions during 14:17–14:29.

The driver accepted the stop with a bare 'Ok' (F12) without confirming the location, which under RD-5 weakens the argument that the rider consented to the Beach Road routing rather than a generic stop.

[F9 F6 F7] [RD-2 RD-3]
→ D2: The pre-departure agreement (14:01/14:02, F10, F11) is on its face a specific routing consent ('by Cavenagh'), and RD-5 only exempts 'that segment' — it cannot exempt kilometres the driver drove 816 m off the optimal route between 14:10 and 14:13, before the Cavenagh routing was even reached. [F10 F11 F4] [RD-5]
→ D3: The 13:52 accident (F17) was on Orchard Road two lanes closed at Cavenagh — i.e. it supports avoiding Orchard Road, not a 2.83 km drive out to Beach Road; and On F4's own numbers that segment did not replace any part of the optimal route (0.00 km covered), so there was nothing to be justified on it. [F17 F4] [RD-4]
→ D4: Band 1 congestion on Orchard Road (F14) ran 14:00–14:10, while the disputed Beach Road segment ran 14:17–14:29 (F5); a traffic record for a road already behind the vehicle cannot justify the later deviation under RD-4(a), and RD-4(b) bands are corroboration only. [F14 F5] [RD-4]
→ D5: The rider consented to 'a 7-Eleven on the way' (F11, F12) with no location named: RD-3(b) says a driver-chosen stop that creates an off-route segment does not exempt those extra kilometres, and RD-3(a) only helps if the stop lay on the optimal route — GPS puts it 2,995 m from pickup and 2,098 m from drop-off at a station reached only via the F5 detour (F2). [F11 F12 F2 F5] [RD-3]
→ D6: The $1.08 is meter waiting time generated entirely by the driver-chosen Beach Road stop at (1.3025, 103.8638), 2,098 m off-corridor (F2, F7); under RD-3(b)/(c) it cannot be excused by a stop request whose chosen location was never named or agreed, and the detour itself is unexempted. [F7 F2] [RD-3]
→ D7: This concedes our core case — 2.83 km unexempted at $1.41/km = $3.99 (F5, F6) — and the only difference from my brief is the extra $1.08 stranded waiting time, which I have justified under RD-3(b)–(c) above. [F5 F6 F7] [RD-2 RD-3]
